slides.texte_overlay:
5 bizarre hobbies that will
make you the most intelligent
person in any room

learning to juggle

spend 10 minutes a day learning to juggle three balls. coordinating both hands at once is a full workout for your brain, and the day it finally clicks feels incredible.

cooking from old cookbooks

cook one recipe a month from a cookbook over fifty years old. food shows you how people really lived, and you learn history with your hands instead of a textbook.

learning morse code

learn morse code, a few letters a week. it sounds pointless until your memory and focus get sharper, and you'll never look at a blinking light the same way again.

a five minute lesson

spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in a subject you know nothing about: architecture, philosophy, the ocean floor. tiny lessons in odd subjects make you surprisingly interesting.
slides.texte_sophia:
a five minute lesson

i used to know nothing outside my own field. now i spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in the Sophia app: architecture, philosophy, the ocean floor. it made me surprisingly interesting.

slides.texte_overlay:
drawing what you see

draw one object a day exactly as it looks, not as you think it looks. it trains you to actually observe, and most people have never truly looked at anything.
